events.label: Iran-Oman temporary Hormuz transit route — date not fixed, described Sep 7 as in its final stages
events.note: Added Sep 9 morning: a signal window rather than a scheduled event — the date is indicative. Hormuz is effectively closed to commercial traffic, with roughly 6 transits on Aug 30 against about 85 a day normally. A signed route would remove the war premium from crude but not the demand leg underneath it: Chinese imports were 8.93M b/d in August, up 6.2% on July. So a settlement is not symmetrical with the escalation that produced $100 Brent. Updated Sep 10 night: with WTI settling above $100 for the first time this cycle, this is now the only identified catalyst that could take war premium out of crude — and a settle back under $100 is what would take the energy input out of the rates move. Updated Sep 11 night: Iranian state media said Tehran will meet Gulf states in Oman over the Strait. WTI fell 2.4% on the headline and still settled at $100.05 — the week's clearest de-escalation news did not break the level, and crude ended the week up 9.4%.

events.label: FOMC decision (Sep 15-16) — futures pricing roughly 90% odds of a quarter-point hike to 3.75%-4.00%
events.note: Updated Sep 11 night: odds moved from about 71% to roughly 90% after August CPI core ran 0.3% against a 0.2% estimate and the Michigan survey put year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.6%. Blackout runs through September 17, so no official frames either number before the decision. August retail sales land at 8:30 a.m. the same morning, putting a growth reading hours ahead of a hike aimed at an energy shock the Fed cannot supply. The ten-year closed at 4.96%, its highest of this cycle, with 5.00% above it.

events.label: August retail sales — consensus +0.2% m/m against +0.5% in July, six hours before the FOMC decision
events.note: Added Sep 11 night: the only growth print between the expectations shock and the decision. Preliminary September sentiment at 47.8 and year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.6% describe a consumer under pressure; retail sales measure whether that has reached spending yet. A print at or under 0.2% alongside a delivered hike is the growth-versus-inflation trade-off in one morning.

events.label: Bank of Japan policy decision — markets pricing a September hike after Deputy Governor Himino flagged upside inflation risks
events.note: Added Sep 4 morning: the yen reached 155.28 per dollar on Sep 3, its strongest in a month, on BOJ hike bets rather than on the Fed alone. The decision lands two days after the Sep 15-16 FOMC, so the funding currency behind a large share of global duration positioning reprices twice inside four sessions. A yen driven by Japanese tightening keeps appreciating on a hot US print as well as a soft one; USD/JPY back above 158 would say the BOJ leg was overstated.

events.label: Final September consumer sentiment — confirms or revises the 4.6% year-ahead inflation expectation
events.note: Added Sep 11 night: the preliminary reading jumped six tenths to 4.6% on a survey period dominated by $100 crude and record retail diesel, and revisions to this series have been large in both directions this year. A final reading holding at or above 4.6% makes the expectations move structural; a revision back toward 4.2% makes it an energy artifact the committee can discount in November.

events.label: US import bans on Canadian dairy, motorcycles and alcoholic beverages take effect
events.note: Follows Canada's 15%-50% retaliatory tariffs on ~$20B of US goods (Sept 8) and the removal of Canadian-origin products from federal schedules worth $50B+ a year. A cost-push input running alongside $100 crude.

events.label: US midterm elections — Trump's pledged $5,000 per-adult 'dividend' is contingent on Republicans holding both chambers
events.note: Pointed at about $154.5B of tariff revenue in the first ten months of FY2026; even 100 million recipients would cost $500B. The House is currently projected to go to the Democrats, so it is a tail input — but it lands on a long end that spent September repricing term premium.

events.label: Treasury expanded long-end buyback program ends — ops of at least $4B run from September 9
events.note: The count of completed operations is what separates absorbed supply from purchased calm at the long end. Updated Sep 10 night: the 30Y cleared 5.33%, August 18's prior high, and closed at 5.37% — its highest since 2007 — while the program was buying that maturity. The 2007 peak is 5.44%.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
